title: EXP-055 — Hello World Part 3 Section 6: FX_Items Standard Refresh Completed Prompt Handler
objective: On the existing User-scoped FX_Items Form, configure exactly one Form event handler for the built-in StdFormRefreshCompleted event, containing exactly one action at sequence 0 with Response Type Prompt and literal Message Text 'Hello World'. Leave Caption blank, use the default icon, allow only an OK response, and specify no Event To Generate. Verify the complete handler and parameters before performing exactly one ordinary Designer Save. Close the clean Designer Form once, reopen it once through the native recent-forms workflow, and verify recovery of the same User-scoped Form and handler definition. Then close the clean inherited FX_Items runtime tab, open the saved FX_Items runtime Form exactly once through Web Client Open > Select Form, and observe whether the automatic Initial Command Refresh causes the Hello World prompt. Capture and dismiss that prompt using its native OK response. Activate FX_RefreshButton exactly once, observe whether the same prompt appears again, capture and dismiss it with OK, and verify the three original item records and disabled Save state remain unchanged. Record missing prompts as failed postconditions rather than retrying. Classify findings observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt3.md Section 6 (05:00–06:03), the accepted EXP-054-R2 experiment record and decisive evidence, and the relevant EXP-037 Prompt handler configuration and persistence evidence before browser interaction.
T1 must be strictly read-only. Call browser_tabs list before the first browser_tabs select in each fresh worker task.
Establish the authenticated DEM Web Client and Designer identities, editing scope User, exact FX_Items Form Name, ScopeType, ScopeName, Initial Command Refresh, and clean Designer and runtime states.

Inspect Details > Event Handlers and record the complete existing handler baseline. Require that no handler for StdFormRefreshCompleted already exists before mutation. Record any other existing handlers without modifying them.

Inspect Details > Components and Form properties to establish the original components, bindings, and layout. Independently confirm exactly one FX_RefreshButton with Type PushButton, literal Caption FX_Refresh, and Events > Primary StdFormRefresh.

Capture native screenshots and accessibility evidence of the pre-change handler list, FX_Items Form identity and User scope, Button properties, Form Initial Command, runtime tab, and absence of authentication or unsaved-change prompts.

Use the supported native Designer Details > Event Handlers > New workflow documented in EXP-037 to configure exactly one handler associated with the existing built-in StdFormRefreshCompleted event. Do not create a custom event.

Configure exactly one handler action at sequence 0, Response Type Prompt, using its supported Parameters dialog. Set Message Text to the exact typed literal Hello World without a string resource. Leave Caption blank, retain the default icon, configure only OK as the response and default response, and leave Event To Generate empty.

Before Save, verify the committed handler row identifies StdFormRefreshCompleted and the single Prompt action. Inspect the actual parameter summary, expected to resemble PROMPT(Hello World) ICON(DEFAULT) RESPONSE(OK()) DEFAULTRESPONSE(OK), and independently read the parameters where the supported UI exposes them. Do not assume the summary proves hidden parameter values.

Before Save, compare the original event handlers, all existing FX_Items components, their bindings, Button properties, layout, and Initial Command Refresh against the T1 and EXP-054-R2 baselines. No unrelated values may change.

Perform exactly one ordinary native Designer Save only after every required handler parameter and preservation check passes. Capture the native Save result and independently verify Save becomes disabled and the handler definition remains intact.

Close the clean FX_Items Designer Form exactly once through its native Form-tab close control, then reopen exactly once through the supported Designer Form-menu recent-forms entry. Verify Name FX_Items, ScopeType User, original ScopeName, one StdFormRefreshCompleted handler with one Prompt action, exact literal message and response parameters, preserved Button properties, Initial Command Refresh, and disabled Save.

Before runtime testing, inspect the inherited FX_Items Web Client runtime Form and verify it is clean, Save disabled, and free of unsafe pending prompts. Close that runtime Form exactly once using its native Form-tab close control, and verify the tab is absent.

Open the saved FX_Items runtime Form exactly once through native Web Client Open > Select Form. Capture the immediate state before any prompt dismissal and observe whether a native Hello World prompt appears following automatic Initial Command Refresh.

If the expected automatic-refresh prompt appears, capture its literal message, available title, icon, response buttons, and FX_Items context. Dismiss it exactly once using its native OK response. If it does not appear, record the failed postcondition without manual refresh, reopening, or retry.

After the automatic-opening observation, verify the three original item records and Save-disabled state. If the runtime is safe and FX_Refresh is available, activate FX_RefreshButton exactly once, regardless of whether the automatic-opening prompt appeared.

Capture the immediate result of the one FX_RefreshButton activation. Verify whether a second native Hello World prompt appears; if present, capture its literal message and available response controls and dismiss it exactly once with OK. If absent, record a failed postcondition without repeating the activation.

Capture the settled runtime state after the permitted prompt dismissal. Compare dumbbell / 45 pound iron / 45.00 / EA, eggs / cage free / 6.99 / DZ, and guitar / natural acoustic / 129.99 / EA against the EXP-054-R2 baseline. Record the native Object count indicator when visible and verify Save remains disabled.

Maintain one experiment record under experiments/ and worker-authored evidence exclusively under evidence/EXP-055/. Capture the complete acceptance matrix, native screenshots, relevant accessibility snapshots, actual prompt behavior, disclosed errors, action counts, and final repository-confinement audit.

Use one fresh untargeted snapshot and at most one corrected visible inspection after a browser-reference failure. If an essential control or postcondition remains unverified, stop and document the blocker rather than widening the procedure.

If an unexpected modal or authentication challenge obstructs testing, preserve the state and document the exact blocker. Only the expected Hello World Prompt with a verified native OK response is authorized for dismissal during the controlled runtime sequence.
out_of_scope: Any Mongoose Form other than FX_Items, except read-only reference inspection of existing experiment evidence.
Creation of a new Form, IDO, SQL table, property class, validator, caption string, or business-data record.
Creating custom Form events or assigning a new Primary Event to FX_RefreshButton.
Any modification to FX_RefreshButton, including Name, literal Caption, Primary Event StdFormRefresh, Tab value, layout, size, or binding.
Changing Initial Command from Refresh or any other existing Form property.
Changing existing component properties, bindings, component order, or layout.
Adding any handler other than the single handler associated with StdFormRefreshCompleted, or adding more than one action to that handler.
Prompt responses other than OK, a nondefault icon, a nonblank Caption, or any Event To Generate.
String resources, scripts, Set Values actions, variables, validators, conditional logic, or other functionality belonging to later Hello World sections.
Opening, reading, or modifying User Preferences or Diagnostics.
Clearing, configuring, or using the Diagnostic Log for this experiment.
Testing alternate standard events, alternate refresh mechanisms, or multiple Button activations.
Manual runtime Refresh, F4, Filter-in-Place, Get More Rows, additional collection queries, or repeat runtime openings.
Runtime Save, New, Delete, or editing any business-field value.
Browser reload, browser restart, authentication recovery, cache invalidation, global-object unload, Form regeneration, FormSync, deployment, or check-in/check-out.
Cross-session persistence, backend event causation, server-side tracing completeness, or database-level durability.
Creating reusable recipes, changing AGENTS.md, modifying unrelated experiments, or starting another experiment.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values

Create, modify, or delete any non-FX_ Mongoose artifact. The standard event name StdFormRefreshCompleted may only be referenced by the handler definition owned by FX_Items; it must not be created or redefined as a separate event.
Create or change any FX_Items or FX_UMs business-data record.
Create more than one new handler or more than one handler action.
Proceed with handler creation if an existing StdFormRefreshCompleted handler is already present or the handler baseline cannot be established.
Create a custom Form event or use an event name other than StdFormRefreshCompleted for the new handler.
Change FX_RefreshButton or its Primary Event StdFormRefresh.
Change FX_Items Initial Command Refresh.
Configure any Prompt Message Text other than the exact literal Hello World.
Assign a string resource, a nonblank Prompt Caption, a nondefault icon, additional response choices, or an Event To Generate.
Save a partial, uncommitted, or ambiguous handler definition.
Perform more than one ordinary Designer Save or save before the complete handler and preservation checks pass.
Close a dirty Designer or runtime Form without a verified and safe native discard decision.
Perform more than one Designer close/reopen or more than one controlled runtime opening.
Activate FX_RefreshButton more than once.
Repeat an absent or failed Prompt test, manually refresh to force a Prompt, or reopen the Form to obtain missing behavior.
Dismiss an unexpected, unidentified, or non-OK-only dialog as though it were the expected Hello World Prompt.
Modify any business field or perform runtime Save, New, or Delete.
Open or change User Preferences or Diagnostics, or clear the Diagnostic Log.
Restart, reload, deliberately reauthenticate, or replace the browser or Mongoose session to recover an interruption.
Use injected browser JavaScript, hidden controls, internal APIs, direct SQL, or unsupported deep links.
Read, print, screenshot, or copy credential or secret values into evidence.
Infer missing Prompt appearances, handler execution, event order, or internal causation from transcript narration or expected behavior.
Modify AGENTS.md, recipes, unrelated project files, unrelated experiment records, or browser-tool infrastructure.
Perform a second recovery attempt beyond the permitted fresh snapshot and corrected visible inspection.
Begin EXP-055 before explicit operator approval of this proposal.

acceptance_checks.description: Read-only preflight proves a usable authenticated DEM Web Client and Designer, exact FX_Items User-scoped identity (Name, ScopeType, ScopeName), Initial Command Refresh, clean Designer/runtime states, and review of the Section 6 transcript, EXP-037 and EXP-054-R2. Screenshots and accessibility evidence identify the Form and scope before mutation.

The pre-change Details > Event Handlers inventory is captured and establishes no existing StdFormRefreshCompleted handler. The original components and Form properties are inventoried, including one FX_RefreshButton with Type PushButton, Caption FX_Refresh, and Primary StdFormRefresh. Evidence identifies the supported handler configuration surface and shows no conflicting handler.

Before Save, exactly one newly configured handler for the existing standard StdFormRefreshCompleted event is visible, containing exactly one sequence-0 action with Response Type Prompt. The native handler row, action row, and editable parameter details are evidenced. No custom event is created.

Before Save, the Prompt parameters are visibly verified as literal Message Text Hello World, blank Caption, default icon, OK-only response and default response, and empty Event To Generate. The committed native action summary is captured. A read-only comparison establishes preservation of existing handlers, components, bindings, FX_RefreshButton properties, and Initial Command Refresh.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Save succeeds with native confirmation, no error or unsafe prompt, and Save disabled afterward. The configured handler, single Prompt action, required parameters, original components, Button properties, and Form Initial Command remain unchanged in post-Save readback.

One ordinary clean Designer Form-tab close removes FX_Items without an unsaved-change prompt. One supported recent-forms reopen recovers the same User-scoped FX_Items version with one StdFormRefreshCompleted handler, one sequence-0 Prompt action, exact Hello World parameters, preserved components and FX_RefreshButton configuration, Initial Command Refresh, and Save disabled. Evidence establishes same-session UI recovery only.

The inherited FX_Items runtime Form is verified clean and closed once without a prompt. The saved FX_Items Form is then opened exactly once through native Web Client Open > Select Form. Immediate screenshots and accessibility evidence establish the correct Form identity and show whether the expected Hello World Prompt appears after automatic Initial Command Refresh. No manual refresh or additional load is performed.

The controlled runtime opening displays a native Prompt whose literal message is Hello World and whose available response is OK only. Evidence captures the Prompt before exactly one native OK dismissal. If the Prompt does not appear, this acceptance check fails and no reopening or retry is permitted.

After the automatic-opening Prompt observation and permitted dismissal, the FX_Items runtime displays FX_Refresh and the original three records: dumbbell / 45 pound iron / 45.00 / EA, eggs / cage free / 6.99 / DZ, and guitar / natural acoustic / 129.99 / EA. Visible values match the previous baseline, Save is disabled, and the native loaded-object indicator is recorded when supported.

Exactly one native FX_RefreshButton activation results in a second visibly captured Hello World Prompt with its OK-only response. The Prompt is dismissed exactly once with native OK. If no Prompt appears following the single activation, this acceptance check fails; no second click or manual refresh is permitted.

Immediate and settled post-activation evidence establishes the original three records and their unchanged business-field values, FX_Refresh still rendered, Save disabled, and no unintended runtime data modification. Any absent native record-count indicator, unexpected prompt, or ambiguous runtime state is documented rather than inferred.

The final evidence and repository audit reconciles exactly one handler, one Prompt action, one Designer Save, one Designer close/reopen, one clean runtime closure, one controlled runtime opening, no more than one automatic-opening Prompt dismissal, one FX_RefreshButton activation, no more than one activation-Prompt dismissal, zero runtime data mutations, zero manual refreshes, and zero Diagnostics or User Preferences operations. All worker-authored changes are confined to the EXP-055 experiment record and evidence/EXP-055/. The final acceptance matrix cites actual verified evidence for AC-1 through AC-11 and records missing Prompts as failed checks. Findings are classified observed only, without cross-session durability or isolated event-causation claims.

initial_instruction: T1 — Read-only preflight for EXP-055. Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt3.md Section 6 (05:00–06:03), EXP-037's native Prompt handler configuration evidence, and the accepted EXP-054-R2 record and decisive evidence. Begin browser interaction with browser_tabs list before the first select. Establish the authenticated DEM Web Client and Designer, exact User-scoped FX_Items identity, Initial Command Refresh, clean Designer/runtime states, and absence of unsafe prompts. Through native Designer Details > Event Handlers, capture the complete existing handler inventory and verify that StdFormRefreshCompleted has no handler yet. Through Details > Components, establish that FX_RefreshButton remains a single PushButton with literal Caption FX_Refresh and Primary StdFormRefresh; inventory the original components, bindings, and Form properties for later preservation comparison. Record the inherited FX_Items runtime state and its original three item records without closing or refreshing the Form. Capture native screenshots, accessibility evidence, exact identity and scope, and an explicit acceptance-gate report under evidence/EXP-055/. Create or update only the EXP-055 experiment record. Perform zero mutations: no new handler, no Save, no Designer close/reopen, no runtime closure/opening, no Prompt activation, and no Diagnostics or User Preferences interaction. Stop after T1 and report whether the preconditions for the single handler mutation are established. If a tab reference fails, use at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection, then document a blocker without broadening scope.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-144135-Rh6I. Rationale: EXP-054-R2 established that the existing User-scoped FX_Items Form has a saved native FX_RefreshButton with Primary Event StdFormRefresh, that the Button recovers across an ordinary Designer close/reopen, and that a single runtime activation is followed by observed StdFormRefresh and StdFormRefreshCompleted diagnostic entries. EXP-037 established a native Form Event Handlers workflow for one Prompt action, including configuration, ordinary Save, and close/reopen recovery, but did not verify runtime prompt execution. EXP-055 combines these established prerequisites to test one new capability: a Prompt handler attached to the existing standard StdFormRefreshCompleted event, with visible runtime behavior during automatic refresh and one Button activation. No Diagnostics changes or additional Form components are necessary. | Operator review 2026-10-11: added exact_values FX_Items, Hello World, StdFormRefreshCompleted (case-sensitive typing guard), deny_browser_javascript, User editing scope. The single pattern match in the brief text is negated ("Do not create a custom event") and ignored by the scope check. Operator decision: no diagnostics in EXP-055 (operator: "continue"). Approval pending from the operator.
